signature_moves.steal: Rig a low tripod camera behind and below the character, shoot the back/glutes filling frame with arms crossed low behind the body; reuse verbatim as a stock 'power reveal' camera setup.
Storyboard any big growth beat as 3-4 consecutive ECU inserts on different muscle groups (bicep->delt->forearm->glute) rather than one wide shot, with escalating SFX between each.

For a compressed transformation beat, composite 3-5 renders of the same pose at increasing scale receding into the background, biggest nearest camera, to fake a 'growth in motion' read without needing N separate panels.

Close every major growth/power beat on a low-angle, near-full-frame standing pose with radiating background light/lines — establish this as the default 'money shot' camera for the pipeline's own climax panels.
For an anger/power beat, punch both fists toward the lens in strong foreshortening with the face just behind/above them and radiating speed-lines.
Composite a small recognizable reference object (a building, a car, a planet) near the figure's feet or hand to instantly telegraph scale without needing a second character.
Give a flex-and-tear moment its own dedicated panel with a single big onomatopoeia rather than folding it into a wider action panel.
Scale the SFX lettering size/repetition (added I's and !'s: RIP->RIIIIIP->RIIIIIIIP) panel-to-panel to nonverbally signal escalating intensity even when the pose itself doesn't change dramatically.

top_steals.prompt_seed: Camera down at worm's-eye level behind and below the figure, looking up a towering back with the arms crossed low behind the body, the head tipped back and small at the top of the frame so the trapezius and rear-delt mass fills the panel.

Camera low and close, staggered ghost-repeats of the same standing pose recede into the distance behind the figure, each one larger and more muscular than the last until the nearest, biggest figure fills the foreground in a double-bicep flex with radiating speed-lines behind him.

Camera low, just below chest height, angled slightly upward as the figure strides forward with both arms flexed out to the sides in a lat-spread pose, radiating speed-lines behind him, filling nearly the whole frame.

Camera at eye height, the figure stands in a three-quarter power pose with one hand near the chin and the other on the hip, weight shifted onto the back leg, sparkles and a radiating burst pattern filling the background behind her silhouette.
Camera at worm's-eye level behind and below a flying figure, arms crossed low behind the back, city rooftops receding tiny below, the back and shoulder mass filling most of the frame.
Camera close at chest height, both fists punched directly toward the lens in heavy foreshortening, the face visible just behind and above them, radiating speed-lines filling the background.
Camera low behind the figure as one arm punches forward into a shattering surface, debris flying, the back and glute mass filling most of the frame, a small startled onlooker in the corner for scale.

Camera at an extreme low worm's-eye angle looking up past a tiny planet at the figure's feet, straddled stance, arms crossed over the chest, head tipped back, a radiating starburst filling the space behind him so the whole body reads as a silhouette against light.
Extreme close crop on a flexing bicep tearing through a sleeve, sharp claw-shaped force lines radiating outward, a small triumphant face inset in the upper corner of the frame.
Camera low and close as the figure lands in a crouch, seen from a three-quarter angle behind and below, impact debris and speed-lines radiating from the point of landing.

avoid.habit: Impossible crossed-arm forearm interlock in the signature rear pose
avoid.why: Reads fine as flat linework but the forearms overlap in ways a rigged 3D figure can't physically replicate; re-block the arm crossing for CGI.

avoid.habit: Claw-shaped radiating force lines drawn directly onto the muscle surface
avoid.why: A 2D FX convention with no 3D equivalent; replace with practical rim light, particle dust, or a post-process glow instead of trying to model the lines.

avoid.habit: Solid-black cape/cloth tearing into hard graphic shapes
avoid.why: Reads as fabric only through flat silhouette; needs an actual cloth simulation with real tear geometry to survive the move to 3D.
A compositing trick, not a single-camera shot; a literal one-shot recreation isn't possible, it must be built as a multi-render composite.

avoid.habit: Halo/glow rim outlining entire figures against the background
avoid.why: A flat ink/shader trick; needs to become genuine rim/backlighting in the 3D render rather than a uniform outline.
